A.biggest_strength: Exceptional pedagogical clarity and freeform parameter exploration, allowing students to input arbitrary initial sequence numbers and payload lengths to observe live arithmetic and wrap-around behavior.
A.biggest_weakness: Broken mobile responsiveness, where a fixed minimum width causes the SVG diagram to clip horizontally, hiding the entire server lifeline and all server states on standard mobile screens.

B.biggest_strength: Outstanding technical depth with live SND.NXT and RCV.NXT state tracking, verified Linux kernel packet capture correlation, and a responsive mobile layout that dynamically adapts its viewBox.
B.biggest_weakness: Higher cognitive barrier due to starting at a completed connection overview, dual navigation controls (scenes vs. step slider), and lack of arbitrary sequence number customization.

structured_output.reasons: Page B wins overall because it delivers a fully responsive, production-quality educational tool with exceptional technical depth. While Page A excels at pedagogical clarity and hands-on parameter manipulation on desktop, it fails critically on mobile viewports by cutting off the server endpoint. Page B adapts cleanly to mobile devices, tracks internal TCP transmission control block state variables (SND.NXT and RCV.NXT), correlates its numbers with real Linux tcpdump traces, and provides rigorous reference notes on real-world TCP edge cases.
